sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal.
3. Heard the arguments of both sides.
NC: 2026:KHC:6529 HC-KAR 4.
Injured claimant met with an accident on 21.04.2023 and filed the claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.

The Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record, granted an amount of Rs.5,86,010/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from date of petition,
till the deposit.
Aggrieved by the said order, he preferred an appeal and mainly contended that he sustained fracture injuries which are grievous in nature and also examined the Doctor as PW-3.
The Doctor assessed the disability as 41.17% to the right lower limb and 20.58% to the whole-body.
But the Tribunal erred in taking the same as 10% and interest is to be enhanced to 9% and the amounts granted under other heads are meager.

Therefore, he requested for enhanced compensation.
5.
Learned Counsel of the respondent stated that PW-2 is not a treated Doctor.
As such, the Tribunal has rightly considered the disability as 10% and it needs no interference.

It is further argued that she was a Tailor and NC: 2026:KHC:6529 HC-KAR there is no functional disability and she is Susheelamma vs Narayanagowda M T on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18750100/
2 continuing her tailoring work.
6. Though it is stated that she was a Tailor and earning Rs.20,000/- per month, she has not filed any income proof.
As she met with an accident in the year 2023, the Tribunal has rightly considered her notional income as Rs.16,000/- per month.
She was aged 50 years as on the date of the accident and the appropriate multiplier applicable is '13'.
Out of the aforesaid injuries, Injury No.1 is grievous and Injury No.2 is simple in nature.

The claimant also examined the doctor as PW-3 and he stated that as follows:
"OPERATION : of ORIF [Open Reduction Internal Fixation] with Distal Femur [Locking NC: 2026:KHC:6529 HC-KAR Compression Plate] with screws done on date :
22.04.2023.
xxx
DIAGNOSIS : COMMINUTED [SUPRA CONDYLAR] FRACTURE LOWER ONE THIRD OF RIGHT FEMUR.
xxx Comminuted Fracture One Third of Right Femur shows UNION with implants in situ.
Narrowing of Medial Half of the Knee joint space with Osteo Arthritis changes seen in Right knee Joint which is clinically and gradually progressive worsening day by day."
As such, he assessed the permanent physical disability of right lower limb as 41.17% and that of the whole-body as 20.58%.
He advised another surgery for removal of the implants from right femur.
But the cost of the surgery is not estimated.
This Court finds it reasonable to take one 1/3rd of 41.17% as 14%, instead of 10%.

So 'loss of future earning capacity' comes to:
Rs.16,000 x 12 x 13 x 14% = Rs.3,49,440/-.
NC: 2026:KHC:6529 HC-KAR 7.
The claimant was hospitalised as inpatient for a period of 7 days.

The Tribunal granted Rs.1,81,410/-
towards Medical Expenses and it is confirmed.

Considering the nature of injuries, occupation,
period of hospitalisation and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.60,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.35,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/-
for transportation, extra-nourishment and attendant charges and the claimant might not have Susheelamma vs Narayanagowda M T on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18750100/
3 attended any other work atleast for a period of three months and the Tribunal rightly granted Rs.48,000 towards 'loss of income during laid-off' which is confirmed.
PW-3, Doctor suggested another surgery for removal of the implants.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant Rs.30,000/- for 'Future medical expenses'.

8. Thus in all, components awarded by this Court are as below:
NC: 2026:KHC:6529 HC-KAR Particulars Amount in Rs.
Loss of future earning 3,49,440/-
 capacity  Medical Expenses 1,81,410/-
 Pain and Suffering 60,000/-
 Loss of Amenities 35,000/-
 Transportation, Extra 30,000/-
 Nourishment & Attendant  Charges  Loss of income during laid 48,000/-
 up period  Future Medical Expenses 30,000/-
 Total 7,33,850/-
9.

Compensation is enhanced from Rs.5,86,010/-
to Rs.7,33,850/- and the enhanced compensation is Rs.1,47,840/-, which carries interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

10. In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2026:KHC:6529 HC-KAR ii.

The judgment and award dated 25.11.2024, passed in MVC No.2946/2023 by the XIII Additional Small Causes And ACJM and Addl.MACT, Bengaluru (SCCH- 15) is modified;
iii. Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the amount of the compensation within one month from the date of this order on such deposit and iv. Appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on the same.
